notes: The registry concept 'ravishment' is archaic in English while 'gwałt' is the living standard clinical and legal term. 'Gwałt' historically meant 'violence or force' broadly (cf. 'gwałtowny' = violent, sudden), with the sexual meaning becoming dominant. Both senses survive in compound forms: 'gwałt na naturze' (violation of nature) remains a non-sexual idiom.

definition: The standard Polish legal and clinical agent noun for a rapist, formed from 'gwałcić' (to rape or violate) with the standard Polish agentive suffix '-ciel.'
notes: More specific than 'sexual_predator' — 'gwałciciel' refers exclusively to a rapist, not to sexual predators in general. The '-ciel' suffix marks the perpetrator of an action (cf. 'nauczyciel' = teacher, from 'nauczyć' = to teach); no ambiguity about the role. No single Polish agent noun covers the broader English 'sexual predator' concept without additional specification.

definition: The standard Polish legal term for sexual assault, encompassing non-consensual sexual acts that may not meet the legal threshold for rape, including groping, coerced sexual contact, and assault short of penetration.
notes: Broader than 'gwałt' (rape) — 'napaść seksualna' covers the full spectrum of non-consensual sexual acts. 'Napaść' (assault or attack) implies physical aggression. The registry's 'indecent_act' is the closest available but frames a misdemeanor-level violation, whereas 'napaść seksualna' is a serious criminal charge. Standard in legal documents and journalism.

definition: Gerund or verbal noun for molestation or harassment; can refer to sexual harassment, child sexual abuse, or any repeated unwanted sexual behavior; borrowed into Polish from international legal terminology.
notes: The term spans from workplace sexual harassment to child sexual abuse depending on context; standalone 'molestowanie' in Polish public discourse often implies the latter. Latin loanword that entered Polish through legal and clinical channels. The full form 'molestowanie seksualne' is used when disambiguation from non-sexual harassment is needed.

definition: The standard Polish formal two-word term for sexual harassment or sexual molestation, specifying the sexual nature of the unwanted conduct; used in legal, journalistic, and institutional contexts.
notes: Usage expanded significantly during the Polish #MeToo discourse (2017–2018), entering mainstream public vocabulary. Covers both workplace sexual harassment and physical molestation of minors; context disambiguates. Carries more institutional weight than the shorter 'molestowanie' alone.

definition: A formal synonym for sexual harassment with a stronger aggressive connotation; 'napastować' (to harass, pester, or assail) derives from 'napaść' (to attack), lending this term more explicit hostility than 'molestowanie.'
notes: Less common in everyday usage than 'molestowanie seksualne'; the 'napaść' (attack) root makes it read as more aggressive and predatory. Polish legal statutes use both terms in different statutory contexts, creating a two-tier system where 'napastowanie' can imply active pursuit while 'molestowanie' implies unwanted conduct more broadly.

definition: Descriptive clinical-legal phrase for non-consensual sexual touching; literally 'touching without consent,' used in legal discourse, sex education, and activist contexts to define the boundary between permitted and criminal contact.
notes: A descriptive phrase rather than a single lexical item; became prominent in Polish consent education following #MeToo. 'Zgoda' (consent) entered Polish sexual-legal discourse as a technical term; 'bez zgody' (without consent) is now a standard legal qualifier. The registry concept 'frotteurism' is the closest available but is a psychopathological framing, whereas 'dotykanie bez zgody' is a victim-centered legal description.

definition: The act of groping — sexually handling someone's body with the hands; covers both aggressive non-consensual fondling and, less commonly, consensual heavy petting, with context determining the charge.
notes: Verbal noun from imperfective 'obmacywać'; the prefix 'ob-' implies covering or surrounding (cf. 'obierać' = to peel all around), giving the word a sense of thorough, all-over handling rather than a single touch. While frotteurism in the registry is specifically non-consensual, 'obmacywanie' can appear in consensual foreplay contexts but leans heavily non-consensual in public discourse.

definition: Perfective verb meaning 'to have groped' or 'to grope as a completed act'; the perfective aspect implies the violation was carried through to completion, adding finality to the accusation.
notes: Perfective counterpart to imperfective 'obmacywać'; aspectual distinction matters in Polish — 'obmacywać' suggests ongoing or habitual groping while 'obmacać' implies a single completed episode. The perfective 'obmacać' dominates accusatory contexts ('obmacał ją' = 'he groped her'), making it the more legally charged form between the two.

definition: Base imperfective verb meaning 'to feel, touch, or grope'; semantically broader than 'obmacywać,' it ranges from non-sexual (feeling in the dark for a switch) to sexual handling, with the sexual meaning activated by context.
english_term: to feel, to grope, to fondle
notes: The most general verb in this lexical family; 'macanie w ciemności' (groping in the dark) is entirely non-sexual. In sexual contexts 'macać kogoś' implies manual handling of a partner's body. Unlike 'obmacywać/obmacać,' the non-consensual framing is not baked in — context and object determine whether it reads as assault or foreplay. Mapped to 'manual_stimulation' rather than frotteurism to reflect this neutrality.

definition: The standard Polish clinical and legal umbrella term for sexual abuse or exploitation, encompassing any non-consensual sexual use of a person — from child sexual abuse to adult coercion — with emphasis on power differential and the instrumentalization of the victim.
notes: The noun 'wykorzystanie' derives from 'wykorzystać' (to use, exploit, or take advantage of), placing instrumentalization at the semantic core. Broader than 'gwałt' (rape) or 'napaść seksualna' (assault) — it is the clinical umbrella encompassing all forms of sexual victimization. No single registry concept covers this breadth: 'ravishment' is too narrow (rape only), 'sex_trafficking' is too specific, 'sexual_predator' names the perpetrator rather than the act.

definition: Sexual exploitation or abuse; the act of using another person for sexual purposes without free and informed consent, typically involving a power imbalance.
notes: Standalone 'wykorzystanie' means 'use' or 'exploitation' generically; sexual meaning requires context or the full compound 'wykorzystanie seksualne'.

definition: Sexual consent; the voluntary, informed, and ongoing agreement to participate in sexual activity.
notes: Adoption of this compound has grown significantly in Polish public discourse post-MeToo (~2017); before then the concept was rarely named as an explicit term.

definition: Without consent; used in legal, clinical, and journalistic contexts to describe sexual acts performed without the other party's agreement.
notes: 'Bez zgody' is a general Polish phrase ('without permission/agreement') repurposed in sexual-rights and legal discourse; not a fixed technical term but universally understood in context.

definition: Sexual coercion; the use of pressure, manipulation, or threats to compel another person into sexual activity.
notes: Legally distinct from 'gwałt' (rape); covers non-physical pressure and manipulation short of physical force; appears mainly in legal texts and NGO materials.

definition: Sexual intimidation; the use of threatening behavior or language to frighten or coerce another person in a sexual context.
notes: Less common than 'molestowanie seksualne' or 'przemoc seksualna'; appears primarily in legal and academic texts rather than everyday speech.

definition: Sexual violence; any act of a sexual nature committed against a person without consent, including rape, assault, and coercion.
notes: Standard umbrella legal and journalistic term; widely used by NGOs and in media coverage of rape and sexual assault cases in Poland.

definition: Sexual abuse; the act of subjecting another person to unwanted sexual acts, especially within a relationship of trust, authority, or dependency.
notes: Carries connotation of ongoing or systemic abuse rather than a single incident; frequently used in contexts of clergy abuse, domestic violence, and child protection.

definition: Perfective crude slang verb meaning to fuck someone; to have sex with someone, framed as conquest or a completed act.
notes: Perfective aspect of 'ruchać'; 'wyruchał ją' = 'he fucked her.' 'Ruchać' is among the most common Polish crude sex verbs, comparable in frequency to 'pierdolić'.

definition: Youth slang verb for having sex; to fuck someone, with a crude or aggressive connotation.
notes: Primarily identified in teen/youth registers ca. 2010–2018; now declining. The base verb 'zaciukać' also means to stab/kill in some dialects, which may intensify the aggressive connotation in sex usage.

definition: Regional youth slang perfective verb for having sex; to have a fuck, often implying a casual or quick encounter.
english_term: to shag, to have a quickie
notes: Primarily southern Polish regional usage; 'fiknąć' literally means to flip or somersault, repurposed as sex slang. Not spreading nationally; stable within its regional register.

definition: Crude reciprocal imperfective verb meaning to fuck each other; vigorous or sustained mutual sexual intercourse.
notes: From 'pierdolić' with na- intensifier prefix and reflexive -się marking mutual action; one of many Polish crude sex verbs in the 'pierdolić' family. The na- prefix adds intensity.

definition: Regional vulgar imperfective verb meaning to fuck; to have sex with someone with crude and often aggressive connotation.
notes: Less universal than 'ruchać' or 'pierdolić'; weighted toward rural and working-class registers; known nationally but used actively mainly in regional speech communities.

definition: Perfective form of rypać; to fuck once, to have sex with someone on a single completed occasion.
notes: Perfective aspect implies a completed single act; 'rypnął ją' = 'he fucked her.' Used interchangeably with rypać where perfective aspect is required.

definition: Verbal noun from rypać; the act of fucking; crude regional slang for sexual intercourse as an ongoing activity.
notes: Nominalized form; 'ostre rypanie' = 'hard fucking.' Less widespread than 'ruchanie' (from ruchać) or 'pierdolenie' (from pierdolić), which dominate nationally.

definition: Literally 'to let oneself be fucked'; passive construction implying willing sexual submission, used pejoratively about someone regarded as sexually available or loose.
notes: The 'dać się' (to allow oneself) construction frames the subject as passive and consenting; typically slut-shaming when said about a woman, but can be neutral in first-person use.

definition: Very crude slang verb meaning to fuck in the ass; to perform anal intercourse, emphasizing penetrative insertion into the anus.
notes: Compound from 'w' (into) + 'dup-' (ass, from 'dupa') + verbal suffix -czyć; the anal meaning is fully transparent to Polish speakers from the morphology.

definition: Perfective regional crude slang verb meaning to fuck someone; to have sex with someone.
notes: Rare; primarily eastern Poland; perfective counterpart to 'bzdyczyć.' Etymology unclear — possibly onomatopoeic or from eastern dialect roots. Largely unknown outside its origin region.

definition: Imperfective regional crude slang verb meaning to fuck; habitual or ongoing sexual intercourse.
notes: Rarer than its perfective counterpart 'nabzdyczyć'; both terms are confined to eastern Polish regional speech and virtually unknown to younger urban speakers nationally.

definition: Literally 'to let oneself be fucked'; passive construction implying sexual willingness or submission; used pejoratively about someone regarded as sexually permissive.
notes: From 'pierdolić', one of the most vulgar Polish sex verbs; the 'dać się' construction is the key marker of passivity and willing submission; standard in slut-shaming register.

definition: Literally 'to beg for sex'; describes someone so sexually desperate that they make their need humiliatingly explicit.
notes: Not a fixed idiom but a transparent compositional phrase; used to mock or pity someone whose sexual desperation has become socially visible. Implied subject is usually male.

definition: Literally 'hungry for it' (feminine grammatical form); idiom expressing intense female sexual craving or horniness.
notes: The feminine adjective 'głodna' grammatically marks the subject as female; the male counterpart is 'głodny tego.' 'Tego' (genitive of 'to') is a vague deictic standing in for sex.

definition: Literally 'hungry for it' (masculine grammatical form); idiom expressing intense male sexual craving or horniness.
notes: The masculine adjective 'głodny' grammatically marks the subject as male; the female counterpart is 'głodna tego.' Both forms use 'tego' as a vague genitive deictic for sex.

definition: Literally 'to fly toward someone'; very common Polish colloquial idiom meaning to fancy, be attracted to, or have a crush on someone.
english_term: to fancy someone, to be into someone
notes: 'Leci na nią' = 'he's into her.' Not inherently sexual — covers romantic attraction and celebrity infatuation as well as sexual desire. One of the most widely used attraction idioms in Polish.

definition: Literally 'to have an appetite for someone'; Polish idiom expressing strong desire or lust directed at a specific person.
english_term: to have the hots for someone, to lust after someone
notes: More intense than 'lecieć na kogoś'; 'chrapka' implies hungry appetite. The phrase is also used for non-sexual coveting (wanting someone's job or possession), but in sexual contexts maps to lust.

definition: Noun meaning strong appetite or craving; in sexual contexts, lust or desire for a specific person.
notes: Rarely appears standalone; almost always in the fixed phrase 'mieć chrapkę na kogoś/coś.' Not exclusively sexual: covers ambition, greed, and covetousness generally.

definition: Sexual fantasies; erotic mental imagery or imaginative scenarios used for arousal or pleasure.
notes: Straightforward compound noun, neither clinical nor crude; listed under age/gender slang because younger speakers use it more freely in casual conversation; the registry lacks a dedicated sexual_fantasy concept, so eroticism is the closest available slug.

definition: In Polish prison slang, a male prisoner forced into sexual submission and used by other inmates; extended broadly as a street insult for any weak, contemptible, or debased man.
notes: One of the harshest words in Polish vernacular; carries extreme honor-shame economy weight in prison culture; has migrated to general street speech as a severe insult for cowardice or submissiveness, somewhat diluting the original sexual meaning.

definition: Prison slang verb meaning to sexually subjugate another male prisoner, typically through anal rape, thereby reducing him to cwel status and establishing dominance.
notes: Primarily prison-specific; carries connotations of coerced sexual domination rather than consensual sex; also used loosely outside prison to mean 'to humiliate or overpower'; derives directly from the noun cwel.

definition: Prison slang verb meaning to alter a prisoner's cwel status through a sexual act: either to restore a former cwel's standing by making him perform a dominant sex act on another, or conversely to complete the process of making someone a cwel for the first time.
notes: Highly ambiguous due to the Polish 'od-' prefix, which can denote either reversal or completion of an action; the specific meaning depends on context; no English concept captures this honor-economy ritual of using forced sex to grant or strip prison status; genuinely novel concept.

definition: Crude slang verb meaning to penetrate sexually, drawn from the literal meaning 'to plant' (as in planting a tree or seedling); applied to decisive penile insertion.
notes: Agricultural metaphor for penetration; the 'za-' prefix adds purposive/completive aspect suggesting deliberate, committed penetration; common in both prison and general street crude speech.

definition: Crude phrasal verb meaning to have sex with someone, literally 'to do someone'; in prison context emphasizes domination and instrumental use of the other person.
notes: Precise structural and connotative parallel to English 'to do someone'; widely recognized outside prison as general crude sexual slang; in prison context the dominance and objectification reading is foregrounded.

definition: Crude phrase meaning to anally penetrate someone, literally 'to take from behind'; used in prison slang for rape and in general crude speech for consensual anal sex.
notes: Literal translation maps cleanly to English 'to take from behind'; in prison context strongly implies non-consensual anal penetration establishing dominance; in civilian use simply denotes anal or doggy-style sex.

definition: Prison and street slang verb meaning to penetrate sexually with aggression, derived from the literal meaning 'to cut into' or 'to score'; implies forceful, predatory intercourse.
notes: Knife/blade metaphor implies aggressive or potentially non-consensual penetration; the primary civilian meaning is 'to carve' or 'to swindle someone,' so the sexual reading is context-dependent; 'na-' prefix adds downward or onto-target directionality.

definition: Crude slang verb meaning to mount and have sex with someone, from the literal meaning 'to cover' (as one animal mounts another); in prison slang used for forced intercourse from above.
notes: Animal-mounting metaphor exploiting the 'covering from above' imagery; the dominant civilian meaning of 'nakryć' is to catch someone red-handed, so the sexual sense is heavily context-dependent and less recognized outside prison slang.

definition: Common sexual euphemism meaning to penetrate, literally 'to enter'; used for penile insertion in vaginal or anal sex across civilian and prison registers.
notes: One of the most widely used Polish sexual euphemisms; crude score is moderate because it is also normalized in non-prison sexual discourse and lacks the aggressive valence of most prison-slang verbs on this list; parallels English 'to go in' or 'to enter.'

definition: Crude verb meaning to impale or skewer sexually, derived from the literal meaning 'to thread onto a spit or spike'; describes aggressive anal or vaginal penetration with a strong violent image.
notes: Among the more graphically violent sexual metaphors in Polish slang; the literal meaning involves threading meat onto a spit, making the image of brutal penetration explicit; used in both prison and general crude speech.

definition: Prison and military crude slang verb meaning to ejaculate, derived from 'prztykać' (to snap or flick with a finger); the 'wy-' prefix signals outward expulsion, evoking shooting or flicking semen out.
notes: Low recognition outside prison and military subcultures; the base verb 'prztykać' means to flick/snap, making this a kinetic metaphor for the expulsive force of ejaculation; relatively rare in mainstream Polish crude slang.

definition: Military term for bayonets repurposed as a phallic double entendre in prison and military slang; the long rigid pointed weapon serves as a coded metaphor for erect penises or acts of penetration.
notes: Used in contexts where overt sexual language is suppressed; 'skrzyżować bagnety' (to cross bayonets) can imply mutual sexual contact; double entendre relies on the bayonet's phallic shape and its penetrative military function; recognition has declined as military culture becomes less dominant in Polish society.

definition: Term for a small-caliber sporting or hunting rifle repurposed as a phallic double entendre in military and prison slang; the long barrel functions as a euphemism for the penis.
notes: Less widely recognized as a sexual term than 'bagnety'; requires explicit context to be read sexually; 'sztucer' is a borrowing from German 'Stutzen' (a short-barreled rifle); the double entendre operates purely on phallic shape without an obvious action metaphor.

definition: Polish prison slang phrase literally meaning 'to drag someone into the bedding/blanket'; denotes the specific act of forcibly pulling another prisoner into one's bunk to sexually assault them and initiate them into cwel status.
notes: 'Materiał' (literally fabric/material) is prison slang for a prisoner's bedding or sleeping area; the phrase encodes the specific physical choreography of Polish prison sexual coercion — the dragging to a private bunk — as a culturally codified ritual act with no single English-language concept equivalent; genuinely novel concept.

definition: Crude slang verb meaning to penetrate deeply and forcefully during sex, from the literal meaning 'to bury' or 'to dig in'; implies sustained, aggressive deep thrusting.
notes: Burial metaphor for deep penetration; the 'za-' prefix conveys completion (fully buried to the hilt); used in both prison and general crude slang; parallels English 'to bury it in her/him.'

definition: Very common crude slang verb meaning to have sex with someone, derived from the literal meaning 'to hit, strike, or whack'; one of the most versatile and widely recognized Polish vulgar terms for sex.
notes: Precise English parallel is 'to bang' — identical percussive/striking metaphor, same crude register, same broad versatility; also used non-sexually to mean to hit something hard; extremely common in Polish crude speech well beyond the prison context.

definition: Crude slang verb meaning to thrust into sexually with sharp force, from the literal meaning 'to drive in' or 'to hammer in' as one would drive a nail; implies a single decisive, forceful act of penetration.
english_term: to drive it in / to hammer in
notes: Construction metaphor (hammering a nail) for forceful penetration; 'w-' prefix encodes inward motion and the perfective aspect signals a single completed act rather than ongoing thrusting; common in both prison and general crude Polish vocabulary.

definition: Crude reflexive slang verb meaning to force one's way into someone sexually, from the literal meaning 'to break in' or 'to invade'; used for forcible penetration with strong connotations of violation and conquest.
english_term: to force one's way in / to break into
notes: The reflexive 'się' particle combined with the violent root 'wedrzeć' (to break in, as a burglar breaks into a building) makes this one of the most explicitly coercive sexual verbs in Polish slang; carries very strong connotations of non-consent or at minimum extreme aggressive dominance.
